svg.text: Every processor model (single-cycle and both pipelines) calls this one ALU class. Division by zero raises DivideByZero.
each node combines its two children:
carries then go back DOWN: Cout = G + P.Cin
2-bit ripple adders at the leaves turn the correct carries into sum bits.
O(log n) levels up, O(log n) down.
n = 32: 18 gate levels, against 64 for ripple carry.
both added at the same time
k = sqrt(32) ~ 6 bits per block (book eq. 8.1). The carry crosses
one multiplexer per block instead of 6 full adders.
O(sqrt n), 17 gate levels: a tie with lookahead at n = 32, because
sqrt(32) = 5.7 and log2(32) = 5. Lookahead wins as n grows.
The U / V datapath, shared by multiply and divide (book figures 8.11 and 8.15)
bit falling out of U becomes the MSB of V
V ends up holding the low 32 bits of the product
MSB of V moves into the LSB of U
U ends with the remainder, V with the quotient
U is 33 bits wide so that adding or subtracting N (or D) can never overflow - book Important Points 9 and 12.
